title: Sweeter Founds Than Music Knows
description: Sweeter Founds Than Music Knows in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 37, “Praise for the incarnation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sweet-er founds than mu-sic knows Charm me, in Em-ma-nuel'S name; All her hopes my spir-it owes To his birth, and cross, and shame.

lines: Sweeter founds than music knows
Charm me, in Emmanuel'S name;
All her hopes my spirit owes
To his birth, and cross, and shame.
When he came the angels sang
"Glory be to God on high,"
Lord, unloose my stamm'ring tongue,
Who should louder sing than I.
Did the Lord a man become
That he might the law fulfil,
Bleed and suffer in my room,
And canst thou, my tongue, be still.
No, I must my praises bring,
Though they worthless are, and weak;
For should I refuse to sing
Sure the very stones would speak.
O my Savior, Shield, and Sun,
Shepherd, Brother, Husband, Friend,
Every precious name in one;
I will love thee without end.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
